translation_notes: Two Namespace(...) -> two @prefix; FOAF/RDF/RDFS/XSD references -> foaf:/rdf:/rdfs:/xsd:. `@graph g` makes g inherit the block's prefixes, so the three g.bind(...) lines disappear (city, dbpo and foaf stay bound, visible in the printed Turtle). Ten g.add((...)) -> one +{ } (the shared subject city:ernesto merged; the blank node stays {bnode}). name/year become "..."^^xsd:string and "..."^^xsd:gYear (constant lexical forms, so the string form is exact).

original.py (and translated.ldpy) differ from the extracted region by one fix applied identically: `.decode("utf-8")` after g.serialize(...) removed - rdflib >= 6 returns str, so the extracted region raised AttributeError before showing the graph. No RDF meaning.

The driver creates data/ (the region writes ./data/lab2_example_rdflib.ttl, the repository's own folder). It compares stdout (the Turtle text with prefix table), the file written (as a graph) and the return value; 6 mutants killed (typed-literal datatype, plain literal, namespace IRI, missing @graph, missing file).
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the ten `g.add` become one `g += [...]` (Graph.__iadd__ takes any iterable of triples), and the two single-use literals `name`/`year` are inlined (their `# lang="en" for language tags` comment kept once above the name triple). The three commented `g.bind` calls stay: a loop over three pairs is not shorter. The commented-out code and the prints are the original's.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: Namespace objects and binds become six `@prefix` + `@graph g` (as in the faithful translation), the ten triples one `+{ }` with `;` on the shared subjects, `a`, and the two constant typed literals `"..."^^xsd:string`/`^^xsd:gYear`.

Exception to the symmetry rule: the reified-statement blank node becomes an anonymous `[ a rdf:Statement ; ... ]` subject inside the `+{ }`, which removes `bnode = BNode()` and its comment; only the island allows it (rdflib has no anonymous-node syntax). The printed Turtle is unchanged (the original's node was already serialised as `[]`).
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: URIRef and OWL are unused; the four rdflib imports merge into `from rdflib import BNode, FOAF, Graph, Literal, Namespace, RDF, RDFS, XSD`.
optimized_header.ldpy: only Graph is still used (prefixes are declared in the function, the blank node is anonymous): `from rdflib import Graph`.
